Commercial emails to businesses
Who I write to.

Only to companies (legal persons), at the company’s public contact email. I do not write to personal email addresses or to sole traders. Before I send commercial messages, I check the list of legal persons that have opted out, kept by the Directorate-General for the Consumer (Law 41/2004, art. 13-B), and I do not write to anyone on that list.
What data.

The company’s public contact email and the source where I found it (for example the company website, Google Maps or the RNAL, the national register of local lodgings). In sample review replies I use only public reviews from your profile, with the author’s first name as it appears on Google, or with no name.
Why, and on what basis.
I use the email only for the commercial proposal, on the basis of legitimate interest (GDPR art. 6(1)(f)).
How many emails.
At most one first email and a single follow-up.
How long.

The contact email and any exchange that gets no reply, or no interest, are deleted 6 months after the last contact. Samples (for example example replies) and anything you send me if we never sign a contract are deleted within 30 days.
How to stop.

Reply “REMOVER” and I will not write again. I record the request on an opt-out list, with only the email address and the date of the request, and I keep that list for as long as the activity continues. The record is what lets me honour your objection (Law 41/2004, art. 13-A, and GDPR art. 21; legal basis: legal obligation and legitimate interest, GDPR art. 6(1)(c) and (f)).

Allergen table and a menu in four languages

The company and the establishment (legal name, company number (NIPC), registered office, and the name and address of the establishment), the name and role of the person who signs the declaration, and the contact email. Dishes, ingredients and allergens come from the owner, in writing. The signed declaration is mostly information about the company: the only personal data in it is the signatory’s (name, role and signature). Allergen information is about the dishes and is not anyone’s health data. I do not need data about the restaurant’s customers.
Why.

To format and translate the information the owner declared, and to keep the declaration the owner signed, confirming they reviewed and approved the final version. The restaurant is the operator responsible for allergen information (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, art. 8).
Legal basis.

For the signatory’s data: performance of the contract (GDPR art. 6(1)(b)) and a legitimate interest in having proof of what was declared and approved (art. 6(1)(f)). The restaurant remains the operator responsible for allergen information (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, art. 8).

The signed declaration and the approved versions are kept for up to 5 years after the contract ends, only as proof. That period matches the limitation period for proceedings over a serious economic offence (5 years, Decree-Law 9/2021, art. 36) and covers the period for non-contractual liability (3 years, Civil Code, art. 498). Working files are deleted within 30 days of final delivery.
A person reviews it.
I do not use machine translation without review: every delivery is read by a person.

Transfers outside the EU

GitHub and Google are in the United States. Transfers rely on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (European Commission adequacy decision of 10 July 2023), where the company is certified, or on standard contractual clauses approved by the Commission (GDPR art. 46).

Using Grok Bot may mean a transfer of data outside the European Economic Area. In that case the transfer is made with the safeguards the GDPR provides, in particular standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission (GDPR art. 46(2)(c)).

VSME Simples
Purpose.
If personal data still arrives.
Sharing.
This section covers the
report-preparation service (the basic module of the voluntary EU sustainability reporting standard). It does not change the sections above.

I collect only aggregated company data, such as energy, water, waste and aggregated headcount. I do not ask for data that identifies an individual worker. In a very small company, even a total can identify someone (for example “1 woman” or “1 accident”). In that case the company aggregates the categories or omits the point, as the standard itself allows in order to protect a person’s privacy (Annex I, point 22(d)), and the report states the omission.
The aim is not to receive personal data. The files I receive are used only to prepare this report, and are not used to train artificial-intelligence models.
If a document nevertheless contains personal data, I process it only on behalf of the client company and according to its instructions, as a processor (GDPR art. 28), and only to prepare the report.
The files received are deleted 90 days after delivery of the final report. Only the invoice and the records the law requires the provider to keep are retained.
These files are not shared.
